# Java service OOM killed repeatedly under steady load

A service restarts every few hours on its own; users see brief error spikes at restart.

An in-memory cache had no eviction policy, so it grew unbounded until the JVM heap was exhausted and the kernel OOM-killer terminated the process.

1. Capture a heap dump and confirm the cache dominates retained heap
2. Add a size/TTL-bounded eviction policy to the cache
3. Set -Xmx explicitly and enable HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError
4. Monitor heap usage across a full traffic cycle

Error Details
```
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space; GC overhead limit exceeded; dmesg: Out of memory: Killed process 1892 (java) total-vm:6120484kB
```
